120	Remember I said that the word "today" appears here
121	once, and also here: "and HaShem has declared today."
122	So let's begin with the Ramban, who starts by explaining the "today":
123	"And HaShem has declared today" – for "this day is for you like the day of
124	Sinai,
125	like the day of Sinai, and HaShem has raised and elevated you through the receiving of
126	the Torah, so that you be for Him a treasured people above all peoples, for only
127	you received the Torah."
128	So there is a correspondence between these two days: the day of
129	the giving of the Torah at Mount Sinai and this day.
130	I'll try to briefly repeat something we spoke
131	about in the past, in Parashat Bechukotai,
132	and in past years also here in Parashat Ki Tavo. A very
133	important point.
134	At Mount Sinai,
135	we'll see in a moment the verses describing
136	the scene at Mount Sinai, or what happened before the giving of the Torah,
137	the Holy One, blessed be He, offers us the Torah through
138	Moshe Rabbeinu,
139	and we said "we will do and we will hear," and we meant it.
140	But as is known, 40 days after the giving of the Torah
141	came the sin of the golden calf,
142	and we did not receive the Torah, meaning we did not receive
143	in practice the tablets; they were broken on the 17th of Tammuz.
144	Now there were two covenants: there was a covenant that was sealed
145	at Sinai,
146	and another covenant at the end of the 40 years, in the Plains of Moav.
147	In the continuation of this parashah, Parashat Ki Tavo, in fact
148	this is the center of Parashat Ki Tavo, but since
149	we spoke about it in past years, I won't repeat
150	it now, the center of the parashah is the Tochachah,
151	the section of rebuke, right: if you listen to its commandments,
152	it will be so, and if you do not listen, it will be otherwise. And it is written
153	there at the end:
154	"These are the words of the covenant that HaShem commanded Moshe to make with the children of Israel
155	in the land of Moav, besides the covenant He made with them
156	at Horeb." So there were two covenants, and the question is why two
157	covenants are needed. The answer, as we said: the first covenant
158	was broken.
